extra.message: User-controlled query parameters are concatenated into a shell command string that is passed to child_process.exec(). In routes/php.js:31-34 the request's 'item' and 'price' values (and the request path) flow into parseFile() as arg1/arg2/fileName, so an attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '&', ';', '|', '$()') to execute arbitrary OS commands on the server. This is remote command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The file name passed to parseFile() is taken directly from the request URL in routes/php.js:30 (getJsonFromUrl(request.originalUrl).path) and concatenated onto this.phpFolder without any normalization or validation. A request such as '/../../etc/passwd%00.php' resolves realFileName outside ./phpFiles/, allowing an attacker to execute/read arbitrary files on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: req.body.username and req.body.password are passed directly into a MongoDB query. Because express.urlencoded({extended:true}) parses qs syntax, an attacker can send 'username[$gt]=&password[$gt]=' which becomes {username:{$gt:''},password:{$gt:''}} and bypasses authentication entirely, logging in as an existing user.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The /admin management interface is exposed with no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated visitor can reach the administrative page and, together with the unprotected /users endpoints, perform privileged operations.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: GET /users/userlist has no authentication/authorization check and returns every user document from MongoDB. Any anonymous client can enumerate all accounts and their stored fields.

POST /users/adduser performs a privileged state-changing operation (creating arbitrary user records) with no authentication or authorization check, allowing anonymous account creation and data injection.
DELETE /users/deleteuser/:id removes arbitrary user records with no authentication or authorization check, so any anonymous client can delete any user by supplying an id.

collection.find({}, {}) returns full user documents, including plaintext passwords and credit-card numbers, to any caller of the unauthenticated /users/userlist endpoint. Sensitive personal and credential data is disclosed.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: User-controlled values returned by /users/userlist (this.username, this.email, this._id) are concatenated into an HTML string without escaping and injected into the DOM via .html(tableContent). A user whose username/email contains markup (e.g. '">') causes stored XSS in the admin interface when the table is rendered.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is hardcoded as "Shh, its a secret!" in source control. Anyone who knows this value can forge/tamper with session cookies and impersonate users.

libxml_disable_entity_loader(false) combined with loadXML(..., LIBXML_NOENT | LIBXML_DTDLOAD) enables external entity resolution on XML built from user-supplied input ($argv[1]). This file is reachable via the /order.php route, so an attacker can read local files such as /etc/passwd through an XXE payload.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The XML parser is configured with libxml_disable_entity_loader(false) and LIBXML_NOENT | LIBXML_DTDLOAD, enabling external entity expansion for attacker-influenced XML. This permits XXE file disclosure (e.g. SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd") when the file is executed.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The password input is rendered with type='text' instead of type='password', so the password is displayed in cleartext on screen and can be observed by shoulder-surfing or captured by browser autofill/screenshot mechanisms.
